Thus Elmsley for αἰφνίδιος [sudden], comparing the gloss of Hesychius | ἀφνιδία: ἀφνίδαν, ἄφνω [sudden: suddenly, suddenly], where Musurus changed ἀφνίδαν [suddenly] into ἀφνιδίως [suddenly], and since the feminine ἀφνιδία [sudden] does not agree with it, Hermann wrote this as ἀφνίδια [sudden things]. Since the tragedians said ἄφνω [suddenly], the adjective ἀφνίδιος [sudden] has nothing objectionable, even though no other examples of it have been found except two from very recent writers, Nicephorus and Pseudo-Callisthenes, mentioned in the Thesaurus vol. 1, 2 p. 2682.
